strings.name: Andrew Barto
strings.summary: Barto studied mathematics and computer science at Michigan and joined UMass Amherst in 1977, exploring reinforcement learning through links between neural networks and animal learning. With Richard Sutton and other collaborators, he studied how agents improve actions through reward feedback and co-wrote a major textbook. He retired as professor emeritus in 2012 and was named with Sutton a 2024 Turing Award recipient in 2025.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He helped establish central concepts and algorithms of modern reinforcement learning, advancing methods for agents to learn from feedback.
strings.facts.f1.label: Research focus
strings.facts.f1.value: Learning in natural and artificial systems, especially reward signals and control.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Mathematics degree, Michigan (1970); computer science doctorate, Michigan (1975).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Learning action through reward
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Sutton, Charles Anderson and others, he developed feedback-based learning and control methods.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Organizing a field in a textbook
strings.highlights.h2.text: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, with Sutton, connects theory, algorithms and examples.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: He and Sutton shared the 2024 award for reinforcement learning's conceptual and algorithmic foundations.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Second textbook edition
strings.timeline.t2.text: He and Sutton expanded coverage of function approximation, policy gradients and neuroscience.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Retirement and emeritus status
strings.timeline.t3.text: He left full-time teaching while maintaining links with learning research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Reinforcement learning textbook
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Sutton, he published the first edition, systematically explaining learning through environmental interaction.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Learning-control paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Sutton and Anderson, he studied cart-pole control using neuronlike adaptive elements.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining UMass
strings.timeline.t6.text: He became a postdoctoral researcher at Amherst, working on neural networks.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Computer science doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: He completed doctoral training at Michigan and continued investigating natural and artificial learning.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned his Michigan degree, providing a foundation for computing research.
